name: Nullentra
description: Nullentra is a comprehensive emotional suppressor that produces near-total affective blunting for a defined window, leaving only baseline cognitive function and sensory processing intact. The user remains fully conscious, capable of complex tasks, and aware of their environment — they simply do not feel anything about any of it. Developed for trauma-response medical teams and high-stress extraction personnel, it has since found a much wider and more troubling user base.
effects: Complete suppression of emotional affect for 6-8 hours
Full retention of cognitive function, motor skills, and memory formation
Elimination of fear, disgust, guilt, grief, and empathic responses
Users describe it as watching their own life through bulletproof glass
Maintains physiological stress responses (adrenaline) while removing psychological distress
side_effects: Post-dose emotional flood as suppression lifts — can be overwhelming
Memory of actions taken under Nullentra retained in full, without emotional buffering
Repeated use causes lasting emotional blunting between doses
High risk of moral injury — users remember exactly what they did and why it didn't bother them
Rare cases of extended affective disorder — emotional return is delayed or incomplete
Classified misuse in interrogation and coercion contexts
cultural_context: Nullentra occupies a deeply uncomfortable space in GLMZ society. Trauma survivors use it to get through anniversaries, funerals, or therapy sessions too raw to face unmedicated. Interrogators and corporate security use it to perform acts they couldn't stomach otherwise. the Gray Zone enforcers use it before violence. Some use it simply to get through a terrible job — waste processing, body recovery, certain Lazarus clinical trial oversight roles. The drug is legal-ish, restricted but obtainable, and everyone pretends not to know what people use it for.
story_hooks: A trauma counselor realizes that one of their patients has been attending every session on Nullentra — fully articulate, fully present, and completely unable to actually heal — and must decide whether to report the misuse or find another way in
A Helix executive who approved Nullentra's release is found dead, with evidence they spent their final weeks on the drug — the investigation reveals what they were trying not to feel
A runner is hired to deliver a Nullentra shipment and realizes mid-job that the destination is not a clinic but a detention facility — and the quantity is enough for an entire staff for a month
